title: Canary Tokens in Training Data: Detecting Fine-Tuning Attacks via Data Poisoning Tripwires

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Canary-based detection of adversarial fine-tuning is a direct, actionable defense mechanism. If canaries survive normal use but degrade under adversarial fine-tuning, it provides a cheap audit mechanism for model integrity.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Embedding canaries in training data and fine-tuning an open-weight model is feasible with medium compute and LoRA. However, designing canaries that are hard to remove without detection requires some sophistication beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: embed canaries, fine-tune adversarially, probe canary survival. Single experiment with measurable outcome. Tightly bounded if limited to one model and one attack type.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
